idiom_name: async queue (items + waiting resolvers) with for await...of drain
implementation_notes: JavaScript is single-threaded, so the classic lock-and-condition structure is replaced by the event loop: an async queue keeps an array of items and an array of pending resolvers, push resolves the oldest waiter (and can itself await while a capacity bound is full), and consumers drain with for await (const item of queue) - async iteration (ES2018) is the language construct that replaces the blocking consumer loop. The same decoupling appears in Node.js streams, where backpressure is the .write() return value plus the 'drain' event (or await pipeline(...)), and one async queue per rate boundary is the idiom; for genuine parallel production use worker_threads instead.
pitfalls: An empty-queue wait is a promise with no timeout: if the producer dies, the consumer awaits forever unless the queue can be closed or rejected.
A synchronous producer loop (no await) never yields, so the consumer never runs - interleave with await or the event loop.
An array-backed queue is unbounded by default; capacity must be part of the API or a burst fills memory.
An error thrown by the consumer aborts async iteration; the iterator's return() runs cleanup, so release resources in finally blocks.

variants.name: Worker threads + MessagePort (Node.js)
variants.implementation_notes: For genuine parallel production and consumption, Node's worker_threads run JavaScript in parallel: a worker produces results and posts them with parentPort.postMessage (or a MessageChannel/MessagePort pair is transferred for direct worker-to-worker hand-off), and the main thread consumes them through 'message' events - structured cloning replaces shared memory, with SharedArrayBuffer/ArrayBuffer transfer for payloads that must not be copied. The runtime's message queue is the buffer; it is not bounded, so backpressure is the caller's job (credit/acknowledgement protocols) and large payloads should be transferred rather than cloned.
pitfalls: postMessage structured-clones data: class instances, functions and streams do not survive, and large payloads should be transferred as ArrayBuffer or shared via SharedArrayBuffer.
Messages queue without bound when the receiver is slower; add credit/acknowledgement flow control or an explicit protocol.
Workers are heavyweight compared to promises; use them for CPU-bound work, not for I/O hand-off the event loop already handles.
